correctness.rationale: The 81-element operation is explicitly defined. Its commutativity/kei laws and determinant defect were checked exhaustively over all 81^3 and 27^4 inputs respectively; the displayed polynomial expansion explains the certificate. Affine projection subquandles are exactly affine F3-subspaces. An independent projected quadruple yields distinct same-fiber values via the determinant, generates an entire 3-point fiber, and multiplication propagates full fibers across W. Conversely a generating tuple must affinely span W. Full-row-rank 3 by (k-1) matrix enumeration and independent choices of 3 lifts prove all-k counts, including sharp k<4. The 2006 free-four-generator size theorem plus the explicit generation yields the automorphism order. The program was replayed from the exact new package.

originality.rationale: The principal all-k affine-spanning criterion and probability law, with the exact free-kei automorphism count, were not found in inspected sources or published research-record searches. Critical stronger 2006 coverage is acknowledged: free on four generators and order 81 are known and do not constitute novelty. Ta 2026 covers the example and free medial structures, Bardakov–Sangare 2026 covers mostly affine automorphism groups, while 1983 trimediality constrains three generators. This is best-knowledge originality only, with the unavailable 1981 source and possibly implicit finite-geometry/aut group formulas recorded as risks.
residual_risks: The original 1981 Kepka–Němec monograph was not directly accessible; it could contain an equivalent generating-tuple enumeration.
An unindexed result on Hall triple systems, free commutative keis or commutative Moufang loops might imply the same all-k rank criterion.
The explicit automorphism-group order could be deduced from an existing full automorphism classification under different group-theoretic language; a broad unpublished source was not ruled out.
No independent audit has been conducted.

value.rationale: The complete generating-tuple distribution and simple affine rank membership test are natural finite-algebra invariants for the smallest nonmedial commutative kei, not an arbitrary finite slice. They give exact random generation probabilities for every tuple length and an explicit count of automorphisms (24564384) of the distinguished four-generator free object. Distinguishing all generating tuples from merely showing one free generating set is mathematically substantive and relevant to ongoing quandle automorphism research.
